claims.text: Replacing laser/electron-beam melting with binder jetting or ink extrusion followed by de-binding and sintering will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed low-thermal-input route will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi components.
The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is produced under inert conditions with minimal oxide contamination.
An extrusion-printed or binder-jetted green body can be de-bound and sintered to produce a densified alloy structure.
An isothermal sintering temperature of approximately 1573 K is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi components with minimum feature sizes around 100 μm.
A de-binding or initial-reduction stage extending to approximately 1073 K is suitable before final sintering.
Mechanical performance can be evaluated at ambient and cryogenic temperatures.
The proposed process will produce a uniform, fine-grained AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Eliminating rapid melting-solidification cycles will minimize thermal gradients.
Minimizing rapid thermal cycling and steep thermal gradients will reduce residual-stress formation.
The low-thermal-input route will limit oxidation.
Isothermal sintering enables inter-particle bonding and interdiffusion.
Isothermal sintering can densify the material without inducing additional thermal stress.
The proposed route will yield lower residual stresses than conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed route will yield a more homogeneous microstructure than conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed route will improve ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed route will increase yield strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
Rapid localized heating and cooling in conventional laser or electron-beam processing causes high residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
The magnitude of residual-stress reduction and mechanical-property improvement remains uncertain and requires experimental validation.
